findings.title: RSS feed content is stored as raw, unsanitized HTML — stored XSS on the forum domain
findings.body: PollFeed takes each feed item's HTML (CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)) and passes it to TopicEmbed.import, which creates the post with cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html] (app/models/topic_embed.rb:22). Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html posts (app/models/post.rb:133), so `cooked` contains the feed markup verbatim with zero sanitization, and it is rendered unescaped (<%= raw post.cooked %> in app/views/embed/best.html.erb:19, and as cooked HTML in the main app). Any <script> or on* handler in a feed item becomes stored XSS executing on the forum domain for every visitor. The CGI.unescapeHTML makes this worse: the XML parser already decodes entities once, so content the feed author properly escaped (e.g. `<script>` in a code sample) is decoded a second time into live markup — even a fully trusted blog can inject live scripts. Note the import_remote path at least whitelists tags/attributes via Readability; the RSS path sanitizes nothing. Feed content should be run through Sanitize (or an equivalent whitelist) before being stored as raw_html.

findings.title: Server-side fetch follows redirects to any host — SSRF past the embeddable_host check
findings.body: TopicRetriever#invalid_host? only validates that URI(embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host, but TopicEmbed.import_remote fetches with `open(url)` (open-uri), which transparently follows HTTP redirects to arbitrary hosts. An open redirect on the allowed host (e.g. http://blog.example.com/out?u=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data or an intranet address) lets an external requester make the forum server fetch internal URLs; the response is then Readability-parsed and published as a public topic, exfiltrating the content. The fetch layer should validate every redirect target against the allowed host or disable cross-host redirects.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer URL — browsers throw and the iframe never resizes
findings.body: The layout calls parent.postMessage({type: 'discourse-resize', height: ...}, '<%= request.referer %>'). The referer is a full URL with a path (e.g. http://blog.example.com/2013/02/post.html), but targetOrigin must be an origin (scheme://host[:port]); Chrome/Firefox throw a SyntaxError ('Invalid target origin') for anything else. As a result the discourse-resize message is never delivered to the parent page and the embed.js auto-resize feature simply never works. The code should post to the referer's origin only. Additionally, the referer is interpolated into a single-quoted JS string and html_escape does not escape apostrophes on all Rails versions this repo supports, so a referer containing a raw ' would also break the script.

findings.title: Loading page self-reload fails the controller's referer check — embed gets stuck on 403
findings.body: The loading page reloads itself every 30s via document.location.reload() so it picks up the topic once the RetrieveTopic job finishes. A programmatic reload sends the iframe's own URL (the /embed/best URL on the forum host) as the Referer, not the embedding page's URL. EmbedController#ensure_embeddable (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:26) compares URI(referer).host to SiteSetting.embeddable_host and raises Discourse::InvalidAccess on mismatch, so the reload gets a 403 and the embed is permanently stuck on an error page instead of showing the newly imported topic. The referer check needs to also accept the forum's own embed URL (or the loading flow needs another mechanism, e.g. message-bus).

findings.title: Feeds without content:encoded crash the hourly job (nil.scrub)
findings.body: For RSS 2.0 feeds that don't provide <content:encoded> — many feeds only ship <description> — SimpleRSS returns nil for i.content, so `i.content.scrub` raises NoMethodError. The hourly PollFeed job dies partway through the feed and all remaining items are skipped every run. Use a fallback such as (i.content || i.description) and guard for nil before calling scrub.

findings.title: absolutize_urls corrupts protocol-relative URLs (//host/path)
findings.body: The relative-URL rewrite treats any href/src starting with '/' as host-relative: a protocol-relative URL like //cdn.example.com/a.png matches `href.start_with?('/')` and is rewritten to http://blog.example.com/cdn.example.com/a.png, producing a broken link. Protocol-relative URLs are common in feed/article HTML. The check should exclude values starting with '//' (and ideally also absolutize paths that don't start with '/', which are currently left relative and break in the forum context).

findings.title: URIs that pass the regex but are invalid crash the whole import run
findings.body: URLs are only validated against /^https?:\/\// before URI(url) is called in absolutize_urls (and open(url) in import_remote). Feed links or embed URLs containing spaces or other characters illegal in URIs (e.g. 'http://example.com/my post.html') pass the regex but raise URI::InvalidURIError here, which is not rescued — in PollFeed this aborts the entire hourly run so no further feed items are imported, and in the RetrieveTopic job it causes repeated sidekiq retries. Validate with URI.parse in a begin/rescue and skip bad items instead of aborting.

findings.title: ADD COLUMN with DEFAULT + NOT NULL rewrites the entire posts table and blocks writes
findings.body: add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false forces PostgreSQL (< 11) to rewrite every row of the posts table while holding an AccessExclusiveLock. posts is the largest table in a Discourse install, so on any sizable forum this migration blocks all posting/reading for minutes during a deploy. Safer pattern: add the column without a default, backfill in batches, then set the default and the NOT NULL constraint.

findings.title: Find-then-create race on embed_url unique index aborts concurrent import jobs
findings.body: import does `TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and later TopicEmbed.create! inside a transaction. Two concurrent jobs for the same URL (a RetrieveTopic job racing the hourly PollFeed, or two RetrieveTopic jobs for staff, who bypass the redis throttle) both see no existing embed and both build a topic and post; the second create! hits the unique index on topic_embeds.embed_url and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing that job — and in PollFeed, aborting the rest of the feed items. Rescue RecordNotUnique/re-check inside the transaction or use an upsert-style create_or_find.

findings.title: Non-atomic setnx + expire can permanently throttle an embed URL
findings.body: retrieved_recently? does $redis.setnx(retrieved_key, '1') followed by a separate $redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60). If the process crashes (or expire raises) between the two calls, the key never expires and retrieve() will treat that embed_url as recently retrieved forever — the topic is never fetched. Use a single atomic SET with an EX option (supported by redis-rb) instead of the two-step dance.

findings.title: Editing an already-released migration and adding force: true
findings.body: This changes the shipped 20131223171005_create_top_topics migration to create_table :top_topics, force: true. Databases that already ran the migration will never re-run it, so the change is a silent no-op there; on fresh or restored setups, force: true will silently DROP and recreate the table (and any data) if it already exists. Released migrations shouldn't be modified — add a new migration instead. The new db/migrate/20131217174004_create_topic_embeds.rb uses force: true too, carrying the same silent-drop risk.

findings.title: Gating tests for feed_polling_url / embed_by_username are vacuous
findings.body: The tests 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' never enable the preceding conditions: feed_polling_enabled? defaults to false in the test env (and the URL is unset in the username test), so execute short-circuits at the first condition and `poller.expects(:poll_feed).never` passes regardless of the condition under test. These specs would still pass if the url/username presence checks were removed entirely. Each gating test should stub all the prior conditions to true so only the condition under test fails.
